messages:
carmen: Heads up — p99 spike on canary after the autotune rollout, seeing tail oscillation on short-seq routes (~1.6s -> 3.1s). Deploy was earlier this morning. @ryan @mike :warning:

deploy-bot: Deployed commit autotune/kv-prefetch@abc123 to canary eng-runtime-1 at 1790123120

infra-bot: Quick metric snapshot (canary eng-runtime-1):
```
p95: 220ms
p99: 3.1s
qps: 1200
microbatch_size_dist: mode=4 mean=6 tail=16
kv_cache.hits: 0.62 -> 0.50
kernels: smallseq:chosen=ft-openmp -> ft-cuda-quant
```

ryan: Can you paste the canary config? suspect microbatch cap change @carmen

carmen: Pasting the config we rolled out:
```
runtime:
  microbatch:
    max_inflight: 16
    min_size: 2
  kernel_autoselect: true
  kv_prefetch: enabled
```

mike: My hunch: kv_prefetch is warming the cache async and creating bursts that change kernel selection path for very short sequences. Those bursts increase queueing + context switches, which pushes tail to the cuda memcpy/lock path. :thinking:

sophia: Pulled a flamegraph from the canary pod. Spikes line up with prefetch activity — heavy cuda memcpy and lock contention in kv_cache.cpp:214
```
# top stacks
cudaMemcpyAsync
kernel_dispatch
kv_cache::ensure_prefetch
mutex_lock
response_serialize
```

anya: Also saw microbatch autobalance assigning size ~12 for short seqs in the canary — that explains longer aggregation latency. Can we cap microbatch for seq_len<=64 to 8?

carmen: I'm going to roll back kv_prefetch on the canary now. Toggle to disabled and re-evaluate p99. If that fixes it we'll do a quick revert. :hammer_and_wrench:

deploy-bot: Updated config for canary eng-runtime-1: kv_prefetch=disabled (rollout id: revert-abc123) — applied to 3 pods

infra-bot: Post-revert snapshot (1m after):
```
p95: 210ms
p99: 260ms
qps: 1180
microbatch_size_dist: mode=4 mean=5 tail=8
kv_cache.hits: 0.61
kernels: smallseq:chosen=ft-openmp
```

ryan: Nice rollback. Follow-ups: (1) add a microbatch ceiling when seq_len<=64, (2) add a kernel_autoselect guard: if kv_cache.miss_rate > 0.4 prefer smallseq kernel.

carmen: Agreed. I'll open a PR with the two safeguards + a small harness to simulate prefetch races in CI. Will also add a telemetry event for kernel switch reasons. :+1:

mike: Ping me for review. We should instrument prefetch start/end and kernel switch decision reasons (so we can correlate in future).

carmen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 — contains: microbatch ceiling, kernel_autoselect fallback threshold, unit tests + local simulator.

anya: Thanks — let's schedule a quick postmortem note in incidents later.

carmen: Will do. Closing this thread for now, monitoring metrics.
